reviews.explanation: The mention 充 appears in annotation 005 (欲令充遣郭氏更納其母充不許為李氏築宅), where 充 is clearly the husband of 郭氏 and 李氏, matching Jia Chong's role in the main text. No contradicting evidence found.

The mention 充 in annotation 001 (妻李氏名婉/婦人集曰充) identifies 充 as the husband of 李氏, which matches Jia Chong's role in the main text where 賈充前婦是李豐女. The annotation explicitly links 充 to being the husband of Li, consistent with the main narrative about Jia Chong. No contradicting evidence.

The mention 充 in annotation 006 (充母栁氏將亡充問所欲言者) refers to the person whose mother is 栁氏. The main text establishes Jia Chong as the central figure, and the annotation context about his mother and wife Li is consistent with the main narrative about Jia Chong's family situation. The reference semantics correctly identifies this as Jia Chong and distinguishes from his mother 栁氏. No contradicting evidence.

The mention 充 in annotation 013 (充憚郭氏不敢迎李) refers to the person who fears 郭氏 and does not dare to welcome back 李. This directly matches the main text narrative where 充 (Jia Chong) is caught between his wife 郭氏 and former wife 李氏. The annotation explicitly describes the same family conflict as the main text. No contradicting evidence.

The mention '充' is an abbreviated personal name for 賈充. The main text repeatedly uses '充' to refer to the same person who is introduced as 賈充 at the start. The candidate evidence from people.json confirms 賈充 as the canonical name. The coreference chain is internally consistent, and the distinct_from mentions (李豐, 李氏, 郭氏, 郭配, 武帝) are all explicitly different individuals in the text. No contradicting evidence found.

The mention '賈充' is the full name of Jia Chong, the main protagonist of this story. The main text opens with '賈充前婦是李豐女' and consistently refers to this person throughout. The candidate evidence from people.json confirms 賈充 as the canonical name. The coreference chain with all '充' mentions is consistent, and the distinct_from mentions are all explicitly different individuals. No contradicting evidence.

The mention '王隱' in annotation 013 refers to the historian/author of 晉書 (王隱晉書). The annotation text '王隱晉書及充别傳並言詔聽' explicitly cites 王隱 as the author of a source work. The candidate evidence from people.json confirms 王隱 as the canonical name. This is the same person as the 王隱 mention in annotation 010. No contradicting evidence.

This is the same person as the 王隱 mention in annotation 013. The distinct_from mentions (充 and 李) are clearly different individuals in the text. No contradicting evidence.

The mention 充 appears in annotation 007 within the title 充别傳 (Chong's separate biography). The main text and all annotations consistently refer to 充 as 賈充 (Jia Chong), the central figure of this story about his two wives Li and Guo. The annotation 007 text '傳曰/充别' explicitly references the separate biography of Jia Chong. All other 充 mentions in this story (annotations 005, 006, 010, 011, 012, 013) refer to the same person — the husband of Li Wan and Guo Pei's daughter, son of Liu. The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-b0e022a941e1c50c4b8a) provides the canonical name 賈充. No contradicting evidence exists. The identity resolution to Jia Chong is well-supported.

The mention 充 in annotation 011 is clearly Jia Chong (賈充). The annotation text '充母栁亦敕充迎李槐怒攘臂責充曰刋定律令為佐命之功我有其分李那得與我並充乃架屋永年' describes Jia Chong's mother Liu instructing him to welcome Li, and Li Huai angrily rebuking him. This is consistent with the main text where 充 is the husband of Li and Guo, the central figure of the story. The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-4e21e21be5b23789a701) provides the canonical name 賈充. The identity resolution is well-supported by the contextual evidence.

This mention is 汝 (the second-person pronoun 'you') in annotation 006, appearing in the speech of 栁氏 (Liu, Jia Chong's mother): '栁曰我教汝迎李新婦尚不肯安問他事'. The pronoun 汝 refers to the addressee of Liu's speech, who is her son — that is, Jia Chong (充). The candidate c0 is 沈充 (Shen Chong), a completely different historical figure. The evidence sfh1-ev-19-xianyuan-013-liu-annotation-006 clearly shows that 汝 in this context addresses 充 (Jia Chong), not 沈充. The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-27571c074f9e9cb1722c) is from a different source (hng2c1-shishuo-10-guizhen-016-liu-annotation-001) and does not support this mention referring to Shen Chong. The identity assessment claims this 汝 corefers with 充 in the same annotation context, which is Jia Chong, not Shen Chong. This is an explicit identity contradiction.

assertions.interpretation: States that Jia Chong's former wife was Li Feng's daughter, establishing the prior marital relationship before the events of the scene.
Li Feng was executed and the marriage was dissolved, with the wife exiled to the border—events preceding the main scene.
Later, upon an amnesty, Li's daughter was allowed to return—this occurs before the main scene but after the divorce and exile.
Jia Chong had already married Guo Pei's daughter before Li's return, establishing the prior remarriage.
Emperor Wu specially permitted Jia Chong to install both as left and right wives—a ruler's decree preceding the scene.
